title: The Kurgan to the Banner: Roerich, the Central Asian Expedition, and the Treaty for Monuments
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Notary's Son and the Kurgans

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, birth on the Nikolaevskaya Embankment
stops.date_confidence: attested; the birth house is Universitetskaya (then Nikolaevskaya) Embankment 25
stops.campa: A son is born to the notary Konstantin Roerich in the house on the Nikolaevskaya Embankment of Vasilievsky Island, across the Neva from the Admiralty. The father is Baltic German and keeps a lawyer's practice; the mother is Russian; the boy is the eldest. They name him Nikolai Konstantinovich. The embankment he is born on runs west past the Imperial Academy of Arts, where he will enroll at nineteen, and east past the university where his father intends him to read law. He will do both at once, and neither profession will hold him.
suggested_refs: The Roerich birth house, Universitetskaya Embankment 25, Vasilievsky Island

stops.name: Imperial Academy of Arts, the double enrollment
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month inferred from the academic calendar
stops.campa: He enrolls in the same season at the university's law faculty, which his father wants, and at the Imperial Academy of Arts, which he wants, and carries both. In the Academy he paints under Arkhip Kuindzhi, who taught light as a doctrine and his students as a brotherhood. In 1897 the Academy gives him the title of artist; in 1898 the university gives him the law degree. He leaves the embankment holding a painter's diploma and a jurist's, and thirty-one years later the second will draft a treaty for the first.
suggested_refs: The Imperial Academy of Arts, Universitetskaya Embankment 17, and Kuindzhi's studio

stops.name: Izvara, the kurgans opened
stops.date_confidence: digging from 1892; the 1899 formulation of the protection idea is attested, month inferred
stops.campa: At the family's country estate west of the capital he has hunted, sketched, and since the age of eighteen dug into the burial mounds of the district, opening kurgans on a permit issued to a schoolboy. The finds go into cases; the notebooks fill. Excavating in the Petersburg province in 1899 he first puts into words the idea that will occupy the rest of his life: that a monument has no defender in law, and that the law must be written. He spends his first twenty-six years in this house, and the house is a museum now.
suggested_refs: The Izvara museum-estate, Volosovsky District, opened 1984

stops.name: Bologoye, Helena Shaposhnikova
stops.date_confidence: year and place attested; month traditional
stops.campa: At an estate at Bologoye, midway on the railway between the two capitals, he meets Helena Ivanovna Shaposhnikova, daughter of an architect and a relative of the composer Mussorgsky. She reads philosophy; she plays piano to concert standard; she is twenty. The partnership that begins at this house will run forty-eight years and carry two sons, one five-year Central Asian expedition, and fourteen volumes of a teaching she takes down and he renders in paint. He is twenty-five and has just finished arguing that monuments need a law.
suggested_refs: The Putyatin estate at Bologoye, where the meeting is placed

stops.name: Paris, the year in Cormon's orbit
stops.date_confidence: the Paris year under Fernand Cormon is attested; the specific studio address is reconstruction, and the Academie Julian attribution is unsupported
stops.campa: He goes to Paris for a year among the museums, exhibitions, studios, and salons, and works under Fernand Cormon, who taught Van Gogh and Toulouse-Lautrec in his time and teaches by correction rather than by doctrine. Roerich takes what he needs of French Symbolist handling and leaves the rest where he found it. Paris is already the hinge of the European esoteric traffic: Blavatsky worked this city a generation before him, and the Theosophical rooms he will enter in London keep their Paris correspondents. He goes home to marry.
suggested_refs: Fernand Cormon's Paris atelier and its Russian students, 1900-1901

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the marriage
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month inferred
stops.campa: Nicholas Roerich and Helena Shaposhnikova marry in Saint Petersburg. He is twenty-seven and has a painter's title, a law degree, a season in Paris, and a growing name among the archaeologists. She brings languages and a library of philosophy. Two sons follow, George in 1902 and Svetoslav in 1904, and both will spend part of their twenties on the Central Asian road. From this year the work is signed by one of them and made by both: she writes, he paints, and the record of who decided what does not survive as two records.
suggested_refs: The Roerich marriage record, Saint Petersburg, 1901

segments.name: Forty Towns and the Rite of Spring

stops.name: Rostov Veliky, forty towns and ninety canvases
stops.date_confidence: tour attested 1903-1904; the Architectural Studies series published 1904-1905
stops.campa: Roerich and Helena set out on a tour of the old Russian towns, some forty of them, Rostov among the first: kremlins, monasteries, and wooden churches painted from the outside in summer light. Nearly ninety canvases come back with them and are gathered as the Architectural Studies. He sees what the survey is really recording. It is a stock of buildings with no standing in law, held by custom alone, and custom does not stop artillery. The conviction he formed over the opened kurgans hardens here into a program.
suggested_refs: The 'Architectural Studies' series, 1904-1905, and the Rostov Kremlin canvases

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the school and the World of Art
stops.date_confidence: directorship from 1906 attested; the World of Art presidency dates to 1910
stops.campa: He takes the directorship of the school of the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and holds it for a decade, rebuilding a drawing academy into a working conservatory of crafts. In 1910 the World of Art society, the circle of Benois and Bakst and Diaghilev that has been remaking Russian taste for fifteen years, elects him president. He is thirty-six: a professor, an archaeologist, an administrator, and a painter of a Russia that ended before writing began. He has not yet been further east than the Volga.
suggested_refs: The Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts, Bolshaya Morskaya 38

stops.name: Talashkino, the Church of the Holy Spirit
stops.date_confidence: church built 1903-1906; Roerich's mosaic and mural work c.1908-1914, year within that range inferred
stops.campa: On Princess Maria Tenisheva's estate at Flyonovo south of Smolensk, where a workshop has been rebuilding embroidery, enamel, and carving on peasant models, Roerich takes the church raised over the family vault and covers its west front and its interior with mosaic. The subject he gives it is the Queen of Heaven above the river of life. The church is dedicated to the Holy Spirit and never consecrated for use: the diocese refuses the iconography. It stands at Flyonovo still, a Russian temple the Russian Church would not accept.
suggested_refs: The Church of the Holy Spirit at Flyonovo, Talashkino, with Roerich's west-front mosaic

stops.name: Paris, the Polovtsian camp for Diaghilev
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Saison Russe opens 19 May 1909
stops.campa: Diaghilev brings Russian opera and ballet to Paris and brings Roerich with them. For Borodin's Prince Igor he designs the Polovtsian camp: felt tents, smoke, a steppe horizon under a low sun, the nomad world painted by a man who has read the excavation reports. Paris takes the dances as a revelation of Asia. Roerich has painted the Asia he knows from grave goods and chronicles, not from the road. The road itself is fourteen years off, and it will run across the country these tents are pitched on.
suggested_refs: Roerich's Polovtsian camp designs for the Ballets Russes 'Prince Igor', 1909

stops.name: Theatre des Champs-Elysees, the Rite of Spring
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Stravinsky's music, Nijinsky's choreography, and Roerich's designs open together on the twenty-ninth of May. The scenario is his as much as Stravinsky's: a pagan Slavic spring rite, the elders in a ring, a chosen girl dancing herself to death for the earth. He dresses the company in the shirts and sarafans of his archaeological studies. The audience shouts the orchestra down. The evening becomes the founding scandal of modern music, and the pre-Christian Russia Roerich reconstructed out of burial mounds enters the twentieth century as noise.
stops.quote: I remember how during the first performance the audience whistled and roared so that nothing could even be heard.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, recalling the 1913 premiere of Le Sacre du Printemps, quoted in the Nicholas Roerich Museum biography (roerich.org)
suggested_refs: Roerich's 1913 costume and backdrop designs for Le Sacre du Printemps

stops.name: Petrograd, the revolution and the arts commission
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1917; day not fixed
stops.campa: The February revolution takes the capital, and Roerich, by then the country's most senior figure in arts administration, works at preservation: commissions, inventories, guards posted on palaces and collections while the city changes hands. In 1914 he had petitioned the Russian army high command and the governments of France and the United States for an international agreement to spare monuments in war, and had been answered with nothing. Now the monuments burn at his own countrymen's hands. After October he stops expecting the new regime to protect anything.
suggested_refs: The 1917 Petrograd arts-preservation commissions and Roerich's 1914 appeal to the high command

segments.name: The Border Closes: Karelia, London, New York

stops.name: Sortavala, the lung and the closing border
stops.date_confidence: move to Serdobol attested December 1916; the exile is created by the 1918 border, not by a departure
stops.campa: A lung condition sends him out of Petrograd to Serdobol on the northern shore of Lake Ladoga, in Karelia, where the air is dry and the granite runs down into the water. He paints the skerries and writes. Then Finland declares independence, the border hardens between the house and the country the house belonged to, and a family that came here for a cure discovers it has emigrated without moving. Nicholas, Helena, and the boys George and Svetoslav will not stand on Russian ground again except on one contested detour, ten years on.
suggested_refs: Roerich's Karelian canvases, Serdobol (Sortavala), 1916-1918

stops.name: London, Covent Garden and the first pages
stops.date_confidence: arrival 1919 attested; the Agni Yoga writing begins in 1920, month inferred
stops.campa: The family reaches London. Roerich designs for Diaghilev at Covent Garden and enters the Theosophical Society, whose Masters in the Himalayan snows have been an article of English occult faith since Blavatsky began posting her letters out of India. In 1920 Helena begins taking down, in a state she describes as dictation rather than composition, the text that becomes the Living Ethics. They call the teaching Agni Yoga. What Blavatsky received from Tibet by post, the Roerichs decide to go and look at with their own eyes.
suggested_refs: Leaves of Morya's Garden, Book One: The Call (Paris, 1923), first volume of the Agni Yoga series

stops.name: Manhattan, the American tour opens
stops.date_confidence: arrival 1920 attested; the tour runs to San Francisco into 1922; the opening gallery is not fixed in the sources used
stops.campa: Roerich lands in New York with more than a hundred canvases and opens a touring exhibition that will cross the country to San Francisco and back over the next two years, stopping at the Art Institute of Chicago on the way. America has no category for him and supplies several at once: Russian master, mystic, theosophist, prophet. It supplies something else as well, which is money. The brokers and lawyers who buy the paintings will fund the expedition, and one of them, Louis Horch, will finance and then dismantle everything Roerich builds here.
stops.quote: The original force of Roerich's work consists in a masterly and marked symmetry and a definite rhythm, like the melody of an epic song.
stops.quote_source: Nina Selivanova on Roerich's painting, quoted in the Nicholas Roerich Museum biography (roerich.org)
suggested_refs: The 1920-1922 Roerich exhibition circuit, New York to San Francisco

stops.name: Santa Fe, the mesas
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Southwest leg is a contested detail of the tour itinerary and the month is not fixed
stops.campa: The tour carries him into the American Southwest and he paints it: mesas cut flat against a hard sky, adobe, the light of a high desert. By his own later account he recognizes the country. It looks to him like the Central Asian plateau he has never seen and has only read about in expedition reports and Tibetan chronicles, and the recognition works on him the way a summons works. He is forty-seven. Within two years he will be in Sikkim with a caravan and permits, testing the resemblance against the ground.
suggested_refs: Roerich's New Mexico canvases and the Santa Fe leg of the 1921 tour

stops.name: New York, the Master Institute of United Arts
stops.date_confidence: founding year attested; the 1921 premises are not fixed in the sources used
stops.campa: He founds the Master Institute of United Arts, a school where painting, music, sculpture, architecture, and drama are to be taught as branches of one discipline, and around it Corona Mundi, an international art center. The doctrine is plain and he repeats it wherever he is asked to speak: culture is the only common language available to nations, and it is cheaper to defend than to rebuild. The institute will not survive 1937. The idea it was built to carry reaches the Oval Office two years before that.
stops.quote: Let us be united, you will ask in what way? You will agree with me: in the easiest way, to create a common and sincere language. Perhaps in Beauty and Knowledge.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, quoted in the Nicholas Roerich Museum biography (roerich.org)
suggested_refs: The Master Institute of United Arts and Corona Mundi, New York, founded 1921-1922

stops.name: Darjeeling, the villa of the exiled Dalai Lama
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Roerichs land at Bombay in December 1923 and are in Sikkim by month's end
stops.campa: The family lands at Bombay and is in Sikkim before the month is out. At Darjeeling they take Talai Pho-Brang, the villa the Thirteenth Dalai Lama occupied during his own exile from Lhasa, and Roerich sets to studying Tibetan painting, hiring men, and buying animals. Seventy years earlier Blavatsky was turned back at this frontier and built a religion out of what she said lay beyond it. Roerich has permits, an orientalist son, American money, and a five-year plan for crossing the country she never entered.
suggested_refs: Talai Pho-Brang villa, Darjeeling, residence of the Thirteenth Dalai Lama in exile

stops.name: Gangtok, the expedition departs
stops.date_confidence: the Sikkim departure is attested to 1924-1925; the month is inferred
stops.campa: The caravan forms in Sikkim and moves north through the Himalayan passes. Roerich paints as he travels, monastery after monastery on their ridges with the snow wall standing behind them, and the Himalayan series begun here will run to hundreds of canvases before the expedition ends. The core party is four: Nicholas, Helena, their son George, who has Tibetan, Sanskrit, Chinese, and Mongolian, and Svetoslav for part of it. The route ahead reads Kashmir, Ladakh, the Karakoram, Chinese Turkestan, the Altai, Mongolia, the Gobi, Tibet.
suggested_refs: The route plan of the Roerich Central Asian Expedition, 1925-1928

stops.name: Srinagar, the Kashmir transit
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1925; month inferred from the marching season
stops.campa: The party crosses Kashmir on the way to Ladakh, and Roerich sketches the Mughal water gardens and the shore of the Dal before the hard stages start. This valley is the standing gateway to the plateau, the last easy country before the caravan trades roads for passes. Blavatsky claimed to have crossed by this same way into Little Tibet behind a Tartar shaman seventy years before, the same Himalayan Masters her Theosophy proposed now doctrinal ancestors of the Agni Yoga Roerich and his wife are building. He enters Kashmir looking for something older than Kashmir.
suggested_refs: The Kashmir-Ladakh caravan corridor, standing approach to the Tibetan plateau

stops.name: Leh, the Namgyal palace and the Karakoram
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1925; month inferred
stops.campa: The caravan reaches Leh under the nine-storey palace of the Namgyal kings, a Tibetan building set on a Ladakhi rock, and Roerich paints it and gathers Buddhist manuscripts. Blavatsky claimed this same corridor in 1856, Kashmir into Ladakh into Little Tibet, and out of the claim she built the hidden Brotherhood in the snows that half of European occultism has believed in ever since. Roerich crosses it with pack animals, a permit, and a son who can read the manuscripts. Ahead lie the Karakoram passes and Chinese Turkestan.
suggested_refs: Leh Palace and the Ladakhi manuscript collections gathered in 1925

stops.name: Khotan, the weeks under guard
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1925-1926; the length of the detention is approximate
stops.campa: At Khotan on the southern rim of the Taklamakan the Chinese provincial authorities decide the expedition is a cover for something else and hold it for weeks, confiscating the weapons and withholding the papers to move on. It is the first of the detentions. Roerich, crossing three empires on a Russian passport that answers to no surviving Russian state, learns here what the rest of the journey will cost in waiting. He keeps the diary that becomes Altai-Himalaya, and he goes on painting under guard.
stops.quote: I am writing only facts. I am setting down fragments of the thoughts as they now live in the East.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, Altai-Himalaya: A Travel Diary (1929)
suggested_refs: Altai-Himalaya: A Travel Diary (1929), Roerich's expedition record

stops.name: Kashgar, the Id Kah and the road east
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1926; month inferred
stops.campa: The party regroups at Kashgar, the old western gate of the silk routes, where the Id Kah mosque fills at Friday prayer and the caravans still sort themselves by destination. From here the road runs east along the northern rim of the Taklamakan through the oasis towns, Karashahr among them, toward Urumchi. Roerich is collecting more than sketches by now. He is collecting prophecies: the local forms of the coming Maitreya, and the names by which the hidden kingdom is spoken of in each valley he passes through.
suggested_refs: The Id Kah Mosque, Kashgar, and the Tarim Basin oasis route

stops.name: Urumchi, papers for the north
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1926; month inferred
stops.campa: Urumchi is the capital of a Chinese province that answers to a warlord rather than to Peking, and the expedition needs it for stamps, provisions, and permission to go north. Roerich gets all three. The route he asks for runs to the Altai and over the Soviet frontier, which for a Russian emigre carrying a Tibetan Buddhist research programme and American funding is not an ordinary request. It is granted anyway. What he intends to do in Moscow is argued over to this day and settled by nobody.
suggested_refs: The 1926 Xinjiang provincial permits for the expedition's northern leg

stops.name: Moscow, the casket of Himalayan soil
stops.date_confidence: the Siberia-to-Moscow detour is attested to 1926; the Chicherin meeting, the casket for Lenin's tomb, and the message from the Mahatmas are scholarly reconstruction (Znamenski, Andreyev), not in the Wikipedia biography
stops.campa: The expedition detours through Siberia to Moscow, and Roerich walks into the foreign commissariat carrying a casket of Himalayan earth for Lenin's tomb and a letter addressed from the Mahatmas of the East to the Soviet government. He leaves paintings behind him in the capital and turns north again for the Altai with the frontier open in front of him. For the rest of his life he is read in three directions at once: as a Bolshevik agent, as an American agent, and as a man following a Buddhist prophecy that answers to no government.
suggested_refs: Andrei Znamenski, 'Red Shambhala' (2011), on the Moscow detour and its purposes
sources: Alexandre Andreyev, 'The Myth of the Masters Revived'

stops.name: Verkh-Uimon, Belukha and Belovodye
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 1926
stops.campa: In the Altai the expedition halts at Verkh-Uimon, an Old Believer village on the Katun, and stays through August. Roerich paints Belukha, the highest peak in Siberia, and writes down what the villagers tell him: that somewhere beyond the passes lies Belovodye, the land of white waters, where the righteous live unmolested and the old faith is kept whole. He sets the Russian legend beside the Tibetan one he has been collecting since Kashgar. The two of them describe the same country from opposite sides of a mountain range.
suggested_refs: The Roerich house-museum at Verkh-Uimon, Altai Republic

stops.name: Urga, wintering under Gandan
stops.date_confidence: wintering attested 1926-1927; month inferred
stops.campa: The expedition winters at Urga, capital of a Mongolia three years into Soviet alignment, under the gilt roofs of Gandan monastery. Roerich moves among Buryat and Mongol lamas, the same network of Tibetan Buddhist intermediaries through which Gurdjieff was rumored to have reached Lhasa before the British guns came, and he takes down the prophecy of the White Burkhan and the approaching age of Shambhala. Helena publishes Foundations of Buddhism here. Beyond the town lies the steppe of Genghis Khan, sealed to outsiders for seven centuries and sealed still.
stops.quote: In a long talk, the lama points out that all may be attained only through Shambhala. For those who imagine Shambhala as a legendary invention, this indication is a superstitious myth.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, Altai-Himalaya: A Travel Diary (1929)
suggested_refs: Gandantegchinlen Monastery, Urga; Helena Roerich, 'Foundations of Buddhism' (Urga, 1926)

stops.name: Tsaidam, the salt crossing
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1927; month inferred from the route
stops.campa: South of the Gobi the caravan crosses the Tsaidam, a basin of salt flats and swamp on the northern shoulder of the Tibetan plateau, at altitude and on shortening supply. Men and animals fail on this stretch, and the diary sets it down as the hardest ground of the journey so far. Ahead lies the Chang Tang, the northern plain, and past it Lhasa, for which the expedition holds passports issued and stamped. Roerich has been on the road three and a half years and is weeks away from the border post that will stop him.
stops.quote: Every obstacle must be the birth of possibilities. When difficulties appear in the face of obstacles, they result precisely from fear... Success lies in the enlarging of the consciousness. It is impossible to come near in the presence of fear.
stops.quote_source: Eastern teaching passage transcribed by Nicholas Roerich in Altai-Himalaya: A Travel Diary (1929)
suggested_refs: The Tsaidam basin crossing as recorded in Altai-Himalaya

stops.name: Chunargen, near Nagchu: five months on the plateau
stops.date_confidence: detention attested from autumn 1927 to March 1928; the campsite is approximate, reconstructed from route descriptions
stops.campa: Tibetan officials halt the expedition on the plain near Nagchu and will not let it advance or withdraw. The party is held through the winter above fifteen thousand feet in summer tents, without fuel and without adequate food, for roughly five months. Five members die. Most of the pack animals die. The passports in Roerich's baggage are valid and are not honored. In March 1928 the party is permitted to leave, southward, away from Lhasa, and the man who came to Asia looking for the hidden kingdom is turned back at the edge of the visible one.
stops.quote: In spite of our having Tibet passports, the expedition was forcibly stopped by Tibetan authorities.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Nicholas Roerich'
suggested_refs: The Chang Tang detention camp near Nagchu, winter 1927-1928

stops.name: Darjeeling, the return
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1928
stops.campa: The survivors come down to Darjeeling and the expedition ends where it was assembled. Five years on the road, thirty-five passes between fourteen and twenty-one thousand feet, some five hundred paintings, and a shelf of ethnographic and linguistic material. Giuseppe Tucci is mounting his own Tibetan expeditions out of the same rail head in these same years, and later scholarship reads the two corpora against each other: the Italian philologist with his manuscripts, the Russian painter with his prophecies, working the same country a decade apart.
suggested_refs: The expedition's closing accounts; roerich.org gives thirty-five passes and about five hundred paintings

stops.name: Naggar, the estate above the Beas
stops.date_confidence: settlement attested to 1928; month inferred
stops.campa: Roerich buys a hillside estate at Naggar in the Kullu valley, below the old raja's castle, with the Beas running in the gorge and the Himalayan wall standing across the north. He is fifty-three and has been in motion for a decade. This is the last address he will have. The family that walked out of Tibet with five of its people dead settles into a house it does not leave, and from the veranda he paints the same range in every light for nineteen years, until the mountains he first painted out of grave goods in Petersburg are the mountains outside the window.
stops.quote: Brother, let us abandon all that rapidly changes... To the eternal.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, poetry fragment quoted in the Nicholas Roerich Museum biography (roerich.org)
suggested_refs: The Roerich Estate at Naggar, Kullu Valley, now the Roerich Art Gallery

stops.name: Urusvati, the institute
stops.date_confidence: founded 1928, active to 1939; month inferred
stops.campa: Beside the house he founds Urusvati, the Himalayan Research Institute, named with a Sanskrit word for the light of the morning star, and Helena takes the chair as honorary president-founder. Its departments are botany, medicine, philology, and archaeology; its collectors go out into Lahaul and Ladakh for plants and manuscripts; its correspondents include Albert Einstein and Robert Millikan. Their son George runs the Tibetan and Sanskrit work. It operates for eleven years on American money and closes when the war cuts the money off.
suggested_refs: The Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute, Naggar, founded 1928

stops.name: Paris, the Pact drafted and the Banner designed
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1929; month inferred
stops.campa: With the international lawyer G. G. Shklyaver in Paris, Roerich turns thirty years of conviction into treaty language: institutions of culture, science, art, and education are to be neutral in war, as hospitals are, and marked as hospitals are marked. He designs the mark himself, a white cloth carrying a red circle with three red circles inside it, and calls it the Banner of Peace. The University of Paris nominates him for the Nobel Peace Prize in the same year, and the nominations come again in 1932 and 1935.
stops.quote: Who would defense a beautiful antique from mad pogroms? It is grievously when the antique dies. But it is more terrible when the antique remains disfigured, false, imitation...
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, 'Silent Pogroms' (1911), as quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Roerich Pact'
suggested_refs: The draft Pact Cultura and the Banner of Peace emblem, Paris, 1929

stops.name: New York, the Master Apartments
stops.date_confidence: attested; the building opens 17 October 1929
stops.campa: The Master Apartments open at the corner of Riverside Drive and West 103rd Street, twenty-nine storeys of brick raised by Louis Horch to house the Roerich Museum, the Master Institute, and Corona Mundi, with rented flats above to pay for the whole. It opens a week before the market falls. Roerich is in the Himalaya and does not see it. Within a few years Horch will claim the building, the collection, and the tax case that goes with them, and the New York institution Roerich built will be taken apart in his absence.
suggested_refs: The Master Apartments, 310 Riverside Drive, opened 17 October 1929

stops.name: Harbin, the seed expedition
stops.date_confidence: expedition attested to 1934; month inferred
stops.campa: The United States Department of Agriculture sends Roerich into Manchuria to collect drought-resistant grasses for the dust-blown American plains, under the sponsorship of Secretary Henry Wallace, who reads his books and addresses him in correspondence as Guru. The expedition bases at Harbin, a Russian-built city on a Chinese river under Japanese occupation, thick with white emigres and their factions. The botanist is looking for grass. The Japanese, the Soviets, and the American press each conclude, separately, that he is looking for something else.
stops.quote: The call about culture, call about the world, and call about creativity and beauty reaches the ear which is strengthen by true values only.
stops.quote_source: Nicholas Roerich, 'Pain of the Planet' (1933), as quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Roerich Pact'
suggested_refs: The 1934-1935 USDA Manchurian expedition and the Wallace correspondence

stops.name: Hailar, the Greater Khingan
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1934; month inferred from the collecting season
stops.campa: The expedition works north-west into the Greater Khingan range and the Barga plateau, along the seam where Manchuria, Mongolia, and Soviet Siberia meet, collecting seed and pressing specimens. It is the most heavily watched frontier in Asia in 1934. Roerich travels it with armed Cossack guards, a son who speaks Mongolian, and letters from Washington, and the Japanese occupation authorities decide they have seen enough of him. The grass collection is real, and it is boxed and shipped west. The suspicions are shipped with it, into three capitals at once.
suggested_refs: The Barga plateau and Greater Khingan collecting stations, 1934

stops.name: The White House, the treaty in the Oval Office
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the fifteenth of April the United States and twenty other republics of the Pan-American Union sign the Treaty on the Protection of Artistic and Scientific Institutions and Historic Monuments in the Oval Office, the first international treaty ever signed in that room. Roosevelt has Henry Wallace sign for the United States. The instrument is called the Roerich Pact everywhere except in its own text, and the man it is named for is two continents away in Inner Mongolia collecting grass seed. Cuba ratifies in August and it enters into force.
stops.quote: The High Contracting Parties, animated by the purpose of giving conventional form to the postulates of the Resolution approved on December 16, 1933... have resolved to conclude a treaty with that end in view, and to the effect that the treasures of culture be respected and protected in time of war and in peace, have agree upon the following articles
stops.quote_source: Roerich Pact, preamble, signed Washington D.C., 15 April 1935; text as reproduced by the Nicholas Roerich Museum (roerich.org/roerich-pact.php)
suggested_refs: The signed instrument of the Roerich Pact, Washington, 15 April 1935

stops.name: The Ordos and the Helan mountains
stops.date_confidence: second season attested to 1935; month inferred
stops.campa: The second season crosses the Inner Mongolian fringe of the Gobi into the Ordos loop and the Helan range, gathering seed stock. In Washington the arrangement is coming apart at the same time: the government botanists on the expedition file complaints, the press begins printing the Guru letters, and Henry Wallace, who sponsored the whole venture, turns on his patron and cancels it. Roerich comes home to Kullu in the year his treaty enters into force and never leaves India again. The Pact stands. The friendship that carried it into the Oval Office does not.
suggested_refs: The 1935 Ordos and Helan Mountains collecting season and its recall

stops.name: Naggar, Nehru and Indira at the house
stops.date_confidence: visit attested to 1942; month inferred
stops.campa: Jawaharlal Nehru comes up to Kullu with his daughter Indira and stays at the Roerich house. India is five years from independence and Nehru is between prison terms. They talk about the Pact and about a cultural union of Asia. For forty years Roerich has argued that a country's monuments are its self-knowledge held in stone, and at sixty-seven he has become, to the family that will govern India, an institution in his own right. His son Svetoslav will marry into the country's cinema. The Roerichs are no longer visitors here.
suggested_refs: The 1942 Nehru visit to the Roerich house at Naggar

stops.name: New York, the American-Russian Cultural Association
stops.date_confidence: founding attested to 1942; month inferred
stops.campa: With the Soviet Union and the United States allied at last, Roerich lends his name to the founding of the American-Russian Cultural Association in New York. He has been called a Soviet agent and a White emigre by turns for twenty years, and now the two governments he was accused of serving are on the same side of a war. He writes from Kullu in support of the Red Army and paints Russian subjects again. The man a border cut off from Russia in 1918 spends the war arguing in public for the country that closed it.
suggested_refs: The American-Russian Cultural Association (ARCA), New York, founded 1942

stops.name: Naggar, the windless day
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Nicholas Roerich dies at Naggar on the thirteenth of December, seventy-three years old, four months after India becomes independent. He is cremated on the slope above the house, facing the range he painted for nineteen years, and a stone is set where the fire stood, cut in Hindi to say that here the body of the great Russian friend of India was given to the flame. Helena is on the terrace above the pyre. She will die at Kalimpong eight years later, still outside the country both of them were born in.
stops.quote: The day of cremation was exceptionally beautiful. Not a single breath of wind and all surrounding mountains were clad in fresh snowy attire.
stops.quote_source: Helena Roerich, on the day of her husband's cremation, quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Nicholas Roerich'
suggested_refs: The cremation stone on the hillside of the Roerich Estate, Naggar

stops.name: New York, the museum on West 107th Street
stops.date_confidence: refounded 1949; month not fixed; the brownstone at 319 West 107th Street is the present address
stops.campa: Two years after his death the institution Horch took apart is refounded in a brownstone on West 107th Street, a few blocks from the tower that had been built for it, under Sina Fosdick, who worked with Roerich from the New York beginning. It holds about a hundred and fifty of his paintings and the archive. Custody of the rest divides and multiplies across the century: two rival Roerich bodies in Moscow, the Russian Museum, the Tretyakov, and collections in Sofia, Thiruvananthapuram, and Bangalore.
suggested_refs: The Nicholas Roerich Museum, 319 West 107th Street, New York

stops.name: The Hague, the Convention
stops.date_confidence: the Convention is dated 1954; the 14 May signing date is the standard date for the instrument and is not stated in the verified pool
stops.campa: The Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict is concluded, and it names the Roerich Pact among its foundations. The blue and white shield it introduces supersedes the Banner of Peace in international law, while the older treaty stays formally in force among the ten states that ratified it. Roerich has been dead seven years. The idea a Petersburg law student took out of an opened kurgan in 1899 is now a standing rule of war, and the wars go on breaking it.
suggested_refs: The 1954 Hague Convention and its Blue Shield emblem

stops.name: Kalimpong, Helena dies
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Helena Roerich dies at Kalimpong in the Darjeeling hills, seventy-six years old, a few marches from the frontier she and her husband crossed in 1924 and never crossed back. The fourteen volumes she took down between 1923 and 1938 are in print in several languages and stay in print. Within four years Tibet is shut, the Fourteenth Dalai Lama comes over these passes into exile, and Miguel Serrano goes up into the same hills to receive him, carrying his own version of the Shambhala the Roerichs went to Asia to find.
suggested_refs: Helena Roerich's Kalimpong residence and her grave in the Darjeeling hills

stops.name: The North Pole, the Banner on the ice
stops.date_confidence: North Pole 6 May 1988 attested; the Mir flight is 11 February 1990 and the South Pole 8 January 2000
stops.campa: A Banner of Peace is carried to the North Pole in May 1988 and planted on the ice. On the eleventh of February 1990 the cosmonauts Anatoly Solovyev and Aleksandr Balandin take one aboard the orbital station Mir. In January 2000 another goes to the South Pole. Three red circles inside a circle, drawn in a Paris office in 1929 by a painter who wanted museums treated the way hospitals are treated, close the century flown at both ends of the axis and once above the atmosphere entirely.
suggested_refs: The Banner of Peace flights: North Pole 1988, Mir 1990, South Pole 2000
